mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES stays sharply below its recent baseline while TRANSIT also remains depressed, weekday discretionary shopping weakens and RETAIL_REC falls further over the next four weeks. The mechanism is a commuting-demand channel: fewer trips to work reduce incidental retail visits.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining below their last-4-week averages.

mechanism_narrative: A week-over-week drop in TRANSIT below its current low level predicts a further short-run decline in RETAIL_REC because fewer station-linked trips reduce spontaneous shopping stops. The effect should appear within one week and persist for about two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -25 and stays there for one weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline in the week after TRANSIT crosses below -25, or rebounds within two weeks while TRANSIT stays below -25.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM rises while PARKS is less negative or increasing, household errand bundling increases neighborhood trip density, which lifts RETAIL_REC over the next two to four weeks. The claim fails if grocery trips remain high but outdoor activity collapses.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 14-28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated and PARKS stops falling.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES drops by another large weekly step while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, a tightening of movement restrictions is likely suppressing discretionary trips, so RETAIL_REC will move lower over the next four weeks. This is a policy-response mechanism that acts after the restriction signal is visible.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -15 while RESIDENTIAL stays above +15
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline over the following 28 days after WORKPLACES falls below -15 with RESIDENTIAL above +15.

mechanism_narrative: An elevated RESIDENTIAL series with weak TRANSIT implies more time spent at home and fewer out-of-home discretionary trips, which suppresses RETAIL_REC over the next one to two weeks. The channel fails if higher home-stay does not coincide with weaker retail mobility.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases within 14 days even though RESIDENTIAL remains above +12 and TRANSIT remains below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained improvement in PARKS, especially when paired with rising GROCERY_PHARM, indicates warmer or more leisure-friendly conditions that spill over into broader discretionary outings. RETAIL_REC should increase over the next four weeks as outdoor activity normalizes.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve over 28 days despite PARKS becoming less negative and GROCERY_PHARM staying above its recent average.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT begins to recover from a deep negative level, the retail effect should first appear in nearby retail and recreation within one week because trips become easier before work attendance fully normalizes. This is a short-lag commuting rebound signal.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by at least 3 points week-on-week from a level below -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the week after TRANSIT improves by 3 or more points from below -20.

mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES continues to deteriorate while GROCERY_PHARM rises, the pattern reflects substitution from commuting and shopping trips to essential errands, which should keep RETAIL_REC below its prior four-week average over the next four weeks. The signal is strongest under a mobility tightening regime.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds its last-28-day mean over the next 28 days even though WORKPLACES keeps falling and GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated.
